veranderings.rede: A soft-drink bottle has a 'doppie' in Afrikaans; 'deksel' is a lid of a pot or tin.
Same bottle cap as earlier; 'doppie' is the natural word and keeps the two mentions consistent.
'Hanteer dit asof' copies English 'treat it as if'; 'tree op asof' is the idiomatic Afrikaans, same word count, and keeps 'asof'.

veranderings.voor: Sy weet ook hy het die damp ingeasem.
veranderings.na: Sy weet ook dat hy die damp ingeasem het.
veranderings.rede: Written standard uses 'dat' with verb-final order, as the lesson itself does in 'Sy weet dat paraffien brand'; adds one word.

veranderings.voor: die toe bottel kliniek toe en daar hou
veranderings.na: die toegedraaide bottel kliniek toe, en daar hou
veranderings.rede: 'Toe' as an adjective right before 'kliniek toe' is colloquial and confusing; and the AWS comma is needed because 'Sy vat' and 'hulle hou' are two clauses with their own subjects.
Signs 'verskyn' rather than 'kom' in written Afrikaans; same word count, 'gewoonlik' kept.
The previous paragraph is about the bottle and the tin, so naming Willem makes clear who 'hom' is; same word count.

veranderings.voor: Sy kyk weer na hom toe dit aand word.
veranderings.na: Toe dit aand word, kyk sy weer na hom.
veranderings.rede: 'Na hom toe' reads first as 'towards him'; putting the time clause first removes the misreading with the same words.
